correctness.rationale: For \(cd>1\), the axial tangent at \(E_y\) forces \(d(p-a)(a+cB)=Bp\), hence the unique \(p\). Direct exact algebra gives \(H(T)=[ad x/((a+x+cy)(dx+y))]H\). The segment supports the explicit two-sided Möbius orbit. The strict inequalities \(p<a+cB\) and \(B>d(p-a)\) allow use of the 2017 dissertation Theorem 6(b), later published in 2019, as the already-established whole-positive-quadrant global attraction premise. The local Jacobian has eigenvalues \(0,\lambda\) with \(0<\lambda<1\), giving summable multiplicative errors in \(x_n/\lambda^n\); the exact cofactor yields a second summable product and \(H_n=C_H(\kappa A)^n\lambda^{n(n-1)/2}(1+o(1))\). As \(H_n=o(x_n)\), the orthogonal projection eventually falls within the finite segment. Exact rational tests and stable logarithmic accumulation passed; the infinite proof does not rely on finite sampling.

value.rationale: Connecting the natural axial equilibria by an *exactly invariant* straight heteroclinic is a motivated geometric question in a map whose global basins were already classified in 2017. The parameter surface is forced by linearization, not arbitrarily chosen. The all-positive-orbit distance law has a quadratic-in-iteration logarithm \(\lim n^{-2}\log\operatorname{dist}(T^n z,S)=\tfrac12\log\lambda\), quantitatively separating transverse alignment from the geometric axial population loss. The nonzero signed asymptotic constant exists for every off-segment initial condition; no global explicit full-plane solution is claimed.
